No.654/2016, On The File Of The Additional Senior Civil

Of 8% Per Annum On Rs.3,82,584/- From The Date Of
Petition Till Its Realization.

This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The respondent No.1 having sustained accidental injuries when he was traveling on the motorcycle as a pillion rider filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 to award just and proper compensation.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.4,12,584/- at 8% interest per annum.

2. The Insurance company has challenged the liability, primarily on the ground that the first respondent/claimant has been falsely implicated as pillion rider so as to claim compensation which is evident from the MLC register, and also that the FIR was lodged by insured, after one day from the date of alleged accident.
A perusal of MLC Register at Ex.C1 indicated that the claimant sustained injuries due to fall when the motorcycle fell down.
The FIR was lodged by the father of the claimant who is the insured, after one day from the date of the accident.
The police after investigation submitted the charge-sheet at Ex.P7 indicating that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the bike i.e., neighbour of the insured.

The claimant in his examination-in-chief has categorically stated that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the bike, and The Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Imran Khan @ Imran on 10 June, 2024

nothing was elicited in the cross examination to disbelieve his statement and no evidence was produced by the insurance company before the Tribunal to substantiate the claimant did not suffer injuries.
Therefore, the Tribunal after appreciating the evidence on record has rightly fastened the liability on the insurance company to pay Rs.4,12,584/-.
4. I do not find any illegality in the impugned order passed by the Tribunal
however, interest awarded at 8% per annum is on the higher side and the same requires to be modified.
5. The claimant/respondent No.1 is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,12,584/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of deposit till actual realization.
The statutory amount in deposit before this Court to be transferred to the jurisdictional Tribunal.
To this extent the impugned judgment and award dated 03.01.2018 passed by the Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge and Member, Addl. MACT, Hassan stands modified.
Accordingly, appeal stands disposed of.
